# Engine build inputs (WebAssembly)

Files preserved from the packaging research (`wiki/rust-engine.md`, section 7) so the `wasm32-wasip1` build of the `pg_query` crate (libpg_query inside) is reproducible:

- `pg_query-18.0.0.patch`: the diff against `pg_query` 18.0.0, the Postgres 18 parser. That version is not on crates.io yet, so `engine/build.sh --prepare` fetches it from GitHub by commit and checks each archive against a SHA-256: [pganalyze/pg_query.rs](https://github.com/pganalyze/pg_query.rs) at `ad0c87ed`, the head of the branch `pg-18` on 2026-10-11 (pull request 79, "Release 18.0.0"), and the libpg_query commit its submodule names, `c1546e7e`, which is the tag 18.1.0 and the grammar of Postgres 18.6. Two hunks are for WebAssembly: the `build.rs` change that pastes in the `extern "C"` block bindgen drops on wasm targets, and that block (`pg_query-extern_block.rs` is the block, 36 functions captured from a native build's bindings; `pg_query-build.rs` is the full patched `build.rs`). Three are for every target, and set how deeply a statement may nest (`src/stack.rs`, wiki/design.md §23): `libpg_query/src/pg_query_internal.h` lowers the depth of the protobuf libpg_query hands over from 10,000 messages to 1,000, `libpg_query/src/pg_query_outfuncs_protobuf.c` refuses a tree past half that while it builds it, and `libpg_query/src/pg_query.c` lets the stack check use up to 16 MB of a native thread's stack rather than 2 MB. The two commits and their SHA-256s are in `pg_query-source.sh`, which `build.sh` reads, so that a new one changes the engine's fingerprint. When crates.io has 18.0.0, they give way to the crate's version and the patch stays as it is. Until 2026-10-11 the patch was `pg_query-6.2.0-wasm.patch`, against crates.io's 6.2.0 (Postgres 17), with the first two parts alone.
- `stubs/`: the headers libpg_query includes and WASI does not provide (`syslog.h`, `netdb.h`), and `wasi_extra.h`, which `build.sh` includes into every C file: it defines `EHOSTDOWN` and maps `sigsetjmp` and `siglongjmp` to `setjmp` and `longjmp`. Postgres 18's parser needed no new one.
- `Cargo.toml` and `src/main.rs`: the probe crate that proved parse, deparse and the `PG_TRY`/`longjmp` error path under Node's WASI. Its calls take the arguments 18.0.0 added (`parse(sql, 0)`, `deparse(&tree, Default::default())`).

Toolchain: `wasi-sdk` 34 (`CC` and `AR` from its `bin/`, `--sysroot` from its `share/wasi-sysroot`, `-I stubs`), `rustup target add wasm32-wasip1`, `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1`. The engine crate proper will live next to this directory.
